literal: Decorum to those who possess, are indeed impossible, evil things, even having slipped, with mouth speaking.
translation: For those who possess good conduct, it is impossible to speak evil words, even by a slip of the tongue.
modern: நல்லொழுக்கம் உடையவர்கள் தவறிக்கூடத் தங்கள் வாயால் தீய சொற்களைச் சொல்ல மாட்டார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the deep-rooted nature of good conduct in a person. The word 'ஒழுக்கம்' (decorum or good conduct) is shown as a defining trait that prevents bad behavior. The phrase 'வழுக்கியும்' means 'even having slipped' or 'even by mistake', emphasizing that true decorum is an ingrained habit rather than just a conscious effort. Therefore, for those who possess such character, uttering evil words with their mouth is simply impossible ('ஒல்லாவே').
